A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAG study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original PAG benchmarks, online-insertion experiments, component ablations, and parameter studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds memory breakdowns and comparisons under matched construction parameters in Appendices G.4–G.5.

M1.justification: V2 Algorithm 1 truncates deferred PES candidates to the nearest 2M per node and restricts final edge additions to available out-degree slots. V1 collected surviving edges without these explicit restrictions. A shared orthogonal transform also becomes explicit in construction and search; the core PRT, TFB, and PES formulas remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six modern and six legacy datasets, including the existing OOD text-to-image and interleaved insertion/search scenarios. The new construction-parameter comparisons retain this coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain HNSW, Vamana, IVFPQFS, ScaNN, RaBitQ+, and SymQG, with the KS2-related PRT-only ablation retained. The added controlled comparisons reuse HNSW and Vamana. Newly cited implementation sources do not establish a change of comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G.5 adds comparisons using matching efC/Lvam values of 200, 400, and 800 across PAG-Base, HNSW, and Vamana. V2 also separates indexing buffer size b=min{efC,100} from the retained search rule b=max{10,K}, replacing v1's generic prescription. These reported changes do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices G.4–G.5 investigate memory composition and whether speed advantages persist under matched construction parameters. These substantially expand analysis of the central memory and efficiency claims. Existing component ablations, parameter sweeps, retrieval-size tests, and online-insertion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, empirical error bars, or significance tests. The added analyses retain point-estimate reporting; revised theoretical probability statements do not change empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds memory-decomposition and matched-parameter results in Figures 20–27. RaBitQ+ curves change on DataCompDr, AmazonBooks, MajorTOM, and DEEP100M at K=10, 100, and 1000. The online-workload plot changes its reported QPS scale by a factor of 10,000 while preserving curve shapes and rankings (v1 Figure 8; v2 Figure 5), without explaining this numerical revision.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix B replace the joint-CLT conditioning argument with explicit conditional-normality and mean-regularity assumptions, uniform block-error conditions, and residual bias/covariance bounds. The concentration argument is revised. Section 4 also changes search/indexing complexity expressions and adds amortized analysis of deferred PES refinement.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain PAG's three components, six practical demands, and up-to-5× speedup claim over HNSW. The revised conclusion emphasizes PAG-Base/PAG-Lite tradeoffs already described in v1, without introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies PRT/PES guarantees as asymptotic approximations away from decision boundaries, whereas v1 asserted the required properties directly. It newly attributes SymQG's high-dimensional failures to unsigned 16-bit overflow and explains smaller PAG dataset payloads through 16-bit vector storage.

D1.justification: V2 specifies stored reference indices, reference-angle cosines, and offset projections in Appendix D, identifies baseline implementations in F.2.1, and confirms actual 16-bit vector storage in G.4–G.5. V1 only suggested two-byte floats as an option. Hardware, Table 4 parameter settings, and the PAG code-access address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds six implementation-source references, including Faiss, hnswlib, Extended RaBitQ, and DiskANN3. The research survey and PAG's positioning relative to PEOs, KS2, and quantized graphs remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most narrative and main-section ordering are retained. Pseudocode discussion and parameter analysis move from Section 4 to Appendices D–E, subsequent appendices are reorganized, and terminology and conclusion wording are refined. Author ordering and corresponding-author information also change.

P2.justification: Figures 20–27 introduce substantial new memory-breakdown and controlled-comparison displays. Retrieval-size figures move into the appendix, algorithms and Table 4 are relocated, and several recall-axis limits and the online-QPS axis change. This materially revises the visual organization beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the matched construction-parameter experiments and memory breakdowns make the efficiency claims easier to assess, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. V2 also qualifies previously broad theoretical statements. However, the revised proof takes the crucial conditional Gaussian approximation as an assumption, and the unexplained 10,000-fold online-QPS rescaling leaves numerical traceability unresolved.
